source: Vinokurova N. Lexical Categories and Argument Structure: A Study with Reference to Sakha. Utrecht, 2005. (LOT Dissertation Series, no. 103)
notes: Joint comitation, on the contrary, implies equal participation in the action by everybody and, hence, imposes no ranking on agents. The underlying predicate must be intransitive (unergative like ytaa ‘cry’, kül ‘laugh’, yllaa ‘sing’) and the subject is always plural. (76) is ambiguous between joint and adjacent readings.
en: i) The children all cried together one after another. ii) ‘The children cried together with someone else. (joint) (adjacent)
